Respondents Revision filed. under Section 397 and 401 of Cr.P.C., praying that in the circumstances stated in the grounds filed against the Judgment of the Il Additional District & Sessions Judge, Kurnool at Adoni, in Cri.A.No.88 of 2007 dated 3% day of July, 2008 The petition coming on for hearing, upon perusing the Petition and the grounds filed in support thereof and upon hearing the arguments of SRI C SHARAN REDDY Advocate for the Petitioner, and of PUBLIC PROSECUTOR for the Respondent, the Court made the following.
ORDER:
THE HON'BLE SMT JUSTICE LALITHA KANNEGANTI eg CRIMINAL REVISION CASE No.990 of 2008 ORDER:-
This Criminal Revision Case arises out of the judgment dated 10.08.2007 passed in Calendar Case No.102 of 2006 by learned Judicial Magistrate of First Class, which was confirmed by common judgment dated 03.07.2008 passed in Criminal Appeal Nos.86 of 2007 and 88 of 2007 by learned II Additional Sessions Judge, Kurnool at Adoni.

sentences.text: The appellants herein who are A-2 and A-3 in C.C.No.102 of 2006 were prosecuted for the offences under Sections 7(i) and 2(ia)(m) punishable under Section 16(1)(a)(i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (for short the 'PFA Act) on the allegation of adulteration of Dilbahar Haldi Powder which was purchased by Gazetted Food Inspector from the shop run by A-1.
3. For the sake of convenience, the parties shall be referred to as they are arrayed in C.C.No.102 of 2006.

4. The facts of the case in nutshell are that on 22.03.2005 at about 3:10 P.M., Gazetted Food Inspector visited the shop which was run by A-1 under the name and style of 'Veeresh Kirana Shop and Cool Drinks' situated on the main road, Urukunda village and found Dilbahar Haldi Power (for short 'powder') packets which were put for sale as food articles to public for human consumption.
A-2 is the supplier and A-3 is manufacturer of said powder.
On the basis of suspicion, the Gazetted Food Inspector purchased six packets and followed the procedure laid down under the PFA Act.

Before completing the process under the PFA Act, when the Gazetted Food Inspector has ensured with A-1l whether he possessed any bill relating to purchase of the powder, he replied in negative; as such panchanama was prepared.

Subsequently, samples of powder were sent to the State Food Laboratory, Hyderabad and in the report the analyst opined that the sample of the powder contains rice starch and therefore, powder is adulterated.
As there was no response from A-3/manufacturer to "the notice as well as the reminder sent under Section 14 (a) of PFA Act, the accused were prosecuted.

After considering the evidence of both the parties, A-1 and A-2 representing A-3 /
manufacturer were found guilty of the offence and were convicted under Section 248 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (for brevity 'Cr.P.C.)) and sentenced.
to undergo Simple Imprisonment for a period of six months and to pay an amount of Rs.1,000/- each as fine in default to suffer further imprisonment for a period of 15 days.

5. Being aggrieved by the same, A-1, who is trader had preferred, Criminal Appeal No.86 of 2007 and A-3 who is manufacturer represented by A-2 / licensee had preferred Criminal Appeal No.88 of 2007 before learned II Additional Sessions, Kurnool at Adoni.

entities.text: II Additional Sessions, Kurnool at Adoni
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The appellate Court upheld the findings of the trial Court and confirmed conviction and sentence passed by the trial Court by observing that the prosecution had proved the necessary ingredients of the provisions of PFA Act.

It was held that the limit of starch prescribed under the Rules of PFA relating to turmeric powder can be up to 60% of the total weight is of a product foreign to the turmeric and haldi is traditional condiment used in every home and cannot be allowed to add 60% of starch.
It is further held that the starch referred therein is the starch of the same haldi but not a foreign starch.
Therefore, termed the powder as adulterated.
Py sg as 6.
Assailing the said order of the lower appellate Court, the present revision is filed by A-2 and A-3.
Heard Sri C.Sharan Reddy, learned counsel for A-2 and A-3 and learned Public Prosecutor for the respondent-state.

sentences.text: Learned counsel appearing for A-2 and A-3 submits that the ingredients to constitute the said offence under Section 16 (1)(a)(i) are not made out and there is no evidence in this respect.

He further submits that the starch contained in the powder is negligible and even as per the report of the analyst, the powder is within the standards prescribed under Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955 (for short the 'Rules) for Turmeric (Haldi) powder in A.05.20.01.
The permissible limit of starch is 60% whereas the total starch contained in the sample powder was 45.62.
Thus,. by no stretch of imagination it cannot be held that the'powder was adulterated.

He also relied upon a judgment of the Madhya Pradesh High Court in Dhanraj Jaiswal vs. State of M.P. through Food Inspector in Criminal Revision No.103 of 2002 dated 05.04.2006, wherein the revision was allowed by setting aside the judgment and order of conviction by observing as under:
"18.

entities.text: Dhanraj Jaiswal vs. State of M.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Gujarat High Court in the matter of Chimanlal Govindji Thakker 1997(2)
FAC 39 also considered the question of microscopic test in respect of the sample of Chillies and observed that, "Having regard to the-aforesaid detail and standard relating to chillies powder, it is clear that microscopic test is not provided therein.
There is, therefore, substance in the submission of Mr. Thakker that the Public Analyst adopted the test by means of microscopic test, which is not provided by the Legislature.
It is also doubtful whether such microscopi test is a scientific test or otherwise.
There is no other evidence available on record, in as much as, there is no method to check such test.
It may be an unreasonable test even.
Suffice it to state the Legislature has not approved was onan of such tests.
Therefore, the conviction of the petitioner for the offence under Section 7 read with Section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act is unsustainable.

23. It is matter of common knowledge that turmeric grinded in bulk then naturally some pieces of cells of that material also grind in the same grinding machine earlier may present which can be observed through such microscopic examination and therefore, mere presence of some cells which are not looking like turmeric cells and resembling like rice starch cells, it cannot be said with certainty that foreign substance have been added in the sample.
In the present case, it was stated by the applicant at the time of taking of sample that he got the turmeric grind somewhere.
This fact has been mentioned in the panchnama (Ex. P-10) shows that the turmeric powder was grind in the factory and therefore, presence.
of foreign rice cell may be there, therefore, it cannot be said that the act of adulterating the foreign substance was done deliberately."

8. ~ Learned counsel for petitioners would submit that in the present case also the analyst has made microscopic examination and found that the turmeric is with plenty of rice starch, which is most unwarranted, beyond the scope and provisions of the Act.

9. Now for better appreciation of the facts of the case it is necessary to extract the prescribed standards that are shown in A.05.20.01 of the Rules, which is as under:

3

entities.text: Shaik Jahangir Pasha And Another, vs The State Of A.P., Rep By Pp
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "A 05.20.01 - TURMERIC (Haldi) POWDER means the powder obtained by grinding the dried rhizomes or bulbous roots of the plant of Curcuma longa L.
It shall be free from artificial colouring matter.

The powder shall conform to the following standards :-
Moisture .......... Not more than 13.0 per cent by weight.
Total ash ...... ... Not more than 9.0 per cent by weight.
Ash insoluble .:'Not more than 1.5 per cent by weight.
in dilute HCI Test for lead chromate ...
Negative Total starch..... , Not more than 60.0 per cent by weight."

10. In view of above rule the limit of permissible starch in turmeric powder is 60% whereas in the case on hand, even according to the report of the analyst, the weight of total starch is comer sine OH rene To, ARON > 45.62% which is less than the prescribed limit.

As rightly contended by learned counsel, the powder cannot be termed as adulterated and further the question of having a microscopic examination is also not permissible and such findings arrived by the Court below deserves to be set aside.

11. In the light of the judgment referred supra and the observations made above, it is clear that the Courts below have committed error in holding the accused guilty for commission of offence charged against them and thus, warrants interference of this Court.

12. Accordingly, the Criminal Revision Case is allowed setting aside the conviction and sentence imposed by the learned Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Adoni in Calendar Case No.102 of 2006 vide judgment dated 10.08.2007 as confirmed by the learned II Additional Sessions Judge, Kurnool at Adoni in Criminal Appeal Nos.86 of 2007 and 38 of 2007 vide common judgment dated 03.07.2008.
